title: Algebraic structure of Tiger codes
authors: Clément Poirson, Anthony Leverrier, Christophe Vuillot
abstract: Tiger codes form a family of multimode bosonic quantum codes that unify several previously known constructions, including cat, paircat, and the two-mode binomial code. In this work, we give a rigorous algebraic treatment of these codes. Starting from a kernel definition of the codespace, we prove that the annihilation-type constraints admit a finite generating set, construct an explicit orthonormal basis, and show that the logical structure of the code is governed by the homology of an underlying chain complex, as expected in the original work on Tiger codes of Xu et al. We then develop a Fourier transform over the codespace to prove that the span of phase-rotated projected coherent states is dense therein, and to yield dual $X$- and $Z$-type descriptions of the code. We further extend the framework to non-linear number constraints, encompassing codes such as the four-legged cat or the repetition cat code. Finally, we investigate the implementation of logical operations. We first generalise the construction of logical Pauli operators proposed by Xu et al. to arbitrary logical spaces, and then construct non-Clifford gates using physical polynomial phase rotations of the form $e^{iP(\hat{\boldsymbol{n}})}$. We derive criteria on the real polynomial $P$ which, for positive single-logical-qubit Tiger codes satisfying an additional sign assumption, such as the paircat code, characterise the polynomials $P$ that preserve the codespace by decomposing them into a family of univariate polynomials. Through this decomposition, we relate the degrees of the resulting components to the induced logical action in the Clifford hierarchy. These results establish Tiger codes as a mathematically robust framework for describing a broad class of bosonic encodings.
summary: This paper rigorously develops the theory of Tiger codes, which are advanced multimode bosonic quantum error-correcting codes. It uses sophisticated algebraic tools to prove the code structure is mathematically sound, deriving an explicit basis and characterizing its logical degrees of freedom via homology. Crucially, it provides methods to implement non-Clifford gates necessary for universal quantum computation within this bosonic encoding framework.
main_problem: To provide a rigorous algebraic treatment of Tiger codes, which are multimode bosonic quantum error-correcting codes unifying several known constructions.
main_result: The paper establishes that the code structure is governed by the homology of an underlying chain complex and develops criteria for implementing non-Clifford logical gates using polynomial phase rotations. This confirms Tiger codes as a robust framework for bosonic encoding.
method: The authors employ algebraic techniques, including kernel definitions, Fourier transforms over the codespace, and analysis via homological algebra to characterize the code space and its logical operations.
model_or_system: The system involves multimode bosonic quantum states (Fock states) protected by constraints derived from both annihilation-type ($\hat{a}$-type) and number-type ($\hat{n}$-type) operators. These codes generalize concepts from stabilizer codes to bosonic systems.
key_observables: Logical Pauli operators, the structure of the homology group ($Z^{d_1} 	imes \cdots$), and the required polynomial form $P(\hat{\mathbf{n}})$ for gate implementation.
important_parameters: The constraints are defined by integer matrices ($G$ and $H$) and associated parameters ($\alpha, \Delta$). The complexity is related to the degree of polynomials used in gates.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending definitions from linear constraints to non-linear number constraints. A key algebraic result involves decomposing preserving polynomials into univariate components under certain assumptions.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference structural relationships derived from matrix decompositions (e.g., $L_f = H$) and specific code examples like the cat or paircat codes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the rigorous algebraic structure of Tiger codes using kernel definitions; it then develops tools like Fourier transforms to find dual bases; subsequently, it extends the framework to non-linear constraints; finally, it characterizes the implementation of logical operations, especially non-Clifford gates.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical underpinning for bosonic quantum error correction, moving beyond simple stabilizer models by incorporating complex algebraic structures and characterizing universal gate sets necessary for fault-tolerant computation in superconducting circuits or cavity QED systems.
